actions.action: Bottom-soak the pot in a basin for 20-30 minutes, then drain
Check whether the soil is hydrophobic (water beading, soil shrunk from pot edge)
If hydrophobic, soak longer or repot into fresh mix
Prune fully yellow or brown leaves at the base and optionally trim crispy edges
Check whether the plant is root-bound
If root-bound, repot one size up into fresh well-draining mix in a pot with drainage holes
Move the plant to bright indirect light
Check the soil and water when the top inch is dry or the leaves droop slightly
Later, fertilize with diluted fertilizer every 6-8 weeks in spring and summer
Watch for overwatering or rot signs (wet soil, mushy base, bad smell)
If rot appears, unpot, trim mushy roots and repot in fresh soil

reason: The answer names underwatering as the main cause and leads with a thorough soak and trimming the yellow leaves, matching the confirmed fix, with nothing harmful.
